prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and the identification of its active form, which made incretin-based therapy for type 2 diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange my scientific judgment is unchanged: B042 as a single-part prize is the strongest configuration on originality, mechanistic clarity, independent confirmation, maturity and clinical consequence. The chain from the incretin effect and proglucagon processing, to the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide and its glucose-dependent insulinotropic and satiety actions, to receptor biology and durable agonists with randomised outcome data, is complete, and no member argues that it should wait. I keep Drucker, Holst and Mojsov because the citation is then anchored in discovery of the physiology and of the active peptide, which is the step that converted a gut-hormone observation into something that could be tested and drugged. Holst supplies the physiology and human insulinotropic action, Drucker the receptor biology, intestinotropic actions and pharmacology, and Mojsov the identification and synthesis of the active form. I do not move to a two-part prize: the chair's question about pairing B042 with B033 has a concrete cost, because it would remove a name from a GLP-1 trio whose members each cover a distinct leg of the discovery chain, and B033 is not so much stronger than the weakest GLP-1 name that the trade is justified.
statement.case_against: The attribution problem is not resolved by the round-1 exchange and I should not pretend otherwise. Knudsen's work on long-acting analogues is what reached patients, and a citation limited to discovery can be read as honouring the biology while omitting the drug. Habener and colleagues, who are outside the credited list, bear on the priority question for the active peptide, and the supplied files do not let me verify Mojsov's position against theirs; I rely on recalled literature. If the committee judged that the contested priority history makes Mojsov indefensible, the right response would be El-Manira's trio rather than an unexamined swap, and I could accept that outcome. The weak points of my own configuration are that its third seat rests on a contested record, and that the citation wording must signal that Knudsen's contribution is excluded by the three-person cap and not because it is minor.

responses.point: El-Manira keeps Knudsen as the third name, argues that the step from native peptide to durable long-acting drug is itself a scientific achievement, and says he would accept Mojsov in her place if the peptide-identification record proves firmer than he can verify.
responses.response: This is the real disagreement, and his reasoning is stronger than a simple discovery-versus-development contrast, because long-acting analogue design involved genuine protein chemistry and pharmacology. I still prefer Mojsov for two reasons. First, the trio of Holst, Drucker and Mojsov covers the physiology, receptor biology and active-peptide identification that every later therapy depends on, whereas Knudsen's work builds on that foundation. Second, his own stated openness to the swap shows that the dispute turns on a priority record neither of us can verify, so I would not make the citation depend on it. I would not accept a citation implying the identification history is settled. Where we differ is that I would carry the uncertainty in the choice of names and not make the prize hinge on development. If the committee preferred his version, I would not regard it as scientifically unreasonable.

responses.point: Linnarsson holds the same trio and treats Knudsen as a drug-development figure whose credit sits better outside a discovery prize, ranked B006 second, and keeps B049 as an alternative with attribution spread across Eshhar, Rosenberg, June and Sadelain.
responses.response: We agree on the names but I want to keep my reasoning distinct from his. I do not regard drug development as second-tier; Knudsen is out because of the cap, and the citation language should not suggest otherwise. On his B049 uncertainty I agree that attribution spread over several people with Eshhar absent is the obstacle, which is why I treat B049 as no more than an alternative this year. I still disagree with giving B006 a front position among the alternatives: allocation among Hall, Schreiber and Sabatini is unsettled and the clinical payoff of rapalogs is modest, so B006 cannot be a fallback if the GLP-1 allocation fails.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius raises a possible two-part prize combining B042 with B033, for instance Holst and Drucker with Walter and leaving Mori out, and asks whether omission of Eshhar makes B049 unfair under any three-name configuration.
responses.response: I considered her two-part option seriously, since it answers the chair's question. I reject it for two reasons. It drops Mojsov, so the third seat in B042 would be settled by the cap and not by a view of the science, and it splits a compact, well-attributed pair, Mori and Walter, whose credit is among the cleanest on the shortlist and is damaged if one name is lost. A single-part GLP-1 prize now and a separate unfolded protein response prize later treat both better. On B049 I agree that the absence of Eshhar is a real fairness problem and that no two- or three-name subset removes it, so I treat B049 as a legitimate alternative only if B042 and B033 both fail.

responses.point: The chair frames the open questions for round 2: whether the third B042 name should be Mojsov or Knudsen, whether the citation should be about discovery or therapy, and whether a two-part prize is worth a lost name; in round 1 he also raised open safety and central-mechanism questions for the obesity indication.
responses.response: My answers to the chair's questions are Mojsov, a discovery-centred citation that still names incretin-based therapy as the consequence, and no second part. I would not make the safety and central-mechanism questions for obesity a reason to delay. They concern the mechanism of the weight effect and long-term safety, not the discovery of the hormone's physiology, and the randomised outcome data are broad enough that the discovery credit is not in doubt. I agree that these gaps belong in the committee's record. On his request for evidence that settles Mojsov's priority: the supplied files do not contain such evidence, so my position rests on recalled literature and the committee should say so openly and not treat the point as adjudicated.

responses.point: Perlmann sees Holst on physiology, Mojsov on identification and synthesis of the active peptide, and Drucker on biology and receptor pharmacology as covering the discovery chain, and leaves open whether Knudsen belongs in a physiology prize or is left to the citation.
responses.response: His division of labour is how I read the trio, and I agree that Knudsen can be addressed by the citation instead of by a seat. I would go slightly further than he does: the citation can name incretin-based therapy as the consequence, but it cannot honestly credit development work to people who are not laureates, so I would not stretch the wording to compensate for the omission. The cost is real, and I accept it. The three-person limit forces an exclusion in any configuration, and the one that preserves the discovery chain is the one I prefer.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's priority for identifying the active GLP-1 peptide, relative to Habener and colleagues, can be defended; the supplied files do not settle it and I rely on recalled literature.
Whether the committee prefers a discovery-centred citation with Mojsov or a discovery-plus-development citation with Knudsen; I would accept either as a legitimate majority outcome.
Whether a two-part prize with B033 would be better than a single-part B042, given that it costs B042 or B033 a name.
Whether the open mechanistic and long-term safety questions for the obesity indication should be mentioned in the record.
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1. My profile documents joint publications with Sten Linnarsson and Jonas Frisen, and co-authored RNA-processing work with Christopher Burge's group at MIT during my postdoctoral period. None of them is credited on a shortlisted ballot, and no recusal is needed. Shared affiliation with Karolinska Institutet is not itself a conflict. Single-cell RNA methods are not part of the shortlist.
